obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact-real model distinguished from deterministic f64 evaluation; finite correspondence only
obernants.assumptions: Declared resource cap, finite inputs and successful allocations
obernants.domain: Finite validated f64 API and separately exact-real target
obernants.observation_scope: Return values, errors, rounded arithmetic and named finite assertions
obernants.operator: Within valid inputs and real candidate outputs, complement contains infeasible or KKT-incompatible pairs and incorrect error outcomes. This is a relational complement of the unique real solution graph, not just a list of negative examples. For the concrete implementation the complement additionally excludes outputs differing from rounded evaluation and includes arithmetic/resource error partitions; real KKT alone is not a full f64 acceptance predicate.

obernants.operator: For interior y (||y||1<r), real preimage is uniquely x=y. On the boundary, x-y=lambda*s with lambda>=0, s_i=sign(y_i) when nonzero and |s_i|<=1 when zero. Thus [3,-1] and [4,-1] both map to [2,0] at r2. r0 has every valid x in the zero fiber; rounded fibers differ.

obernants.operator: Outside the ball, magnitudes satisfy positive-radius simplex domain; sign restoration is an isometry for the relevant orthant. Child mass/rounding failures propagate unchanged; a valid child is necessary but not a universal parent accuracy proof.

obernants.operator: Computed norm<=radius returns input bit pattern unchanged, including signed zeros. Zero radius yields all positive zeros even on extreme finite inputs. Empty vector is feasible for every finite nonnegative radius.

obernants.operator: Validation uses simplex helper and cap. Norm overflow rejects conservatively even if projection exists; radius0 bypasses norm safely. Rounded norm can misclassify a near-boundary point. Failed magnitude or child reservation returns AllocationFailed; no allocation refusal injection.
